sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando* and *en cuanto* from A2 Unit 27, used with the present subjunctive for a future event (*Te llamo cuando termine*), and *tan pronto como* "as soon as" from B1 Unit 37. You also know *apenas* "as soon as" from B2 Unit 2, in stories about the past (*Apenas sonó la alarma, salimos*). This lesson uses all three to look ahead. The rule is the one you know: if the event in the time clause has not happened yet, it is only expected, so Spanish uses the present subjunctive. English uses the plain present for the same idea (*as soon as we arrive*).

sections.title: Not yet happened or already a fact?
rows: As soon as I arrive, I'll call you. (It has not happened yet: subjunctive.)
Tan pronto como tengamos el resultado, te avisamos.
As soon as we have the result, we'll let you know. (Subjunctive.)
As soon as they leave, I'll close the door. (Subjunctive.)
As soon as he arrived, he called me. (A past fact: indicative.)
Tan pronto como llega a casa, llama a su madre.
As soon as he gets home, he phones his mother. (A habit: indicative.)

items.spanish: Tan pronto como termine la reunión, te llamo.
items.english: As soon as the meeting ends, I'll call you.

items.spanish: En cuanto lleguemos al hotel, vamos a cenar.
items.english: As soon as we get to the hotel, we're going to have dinner.

items.spanish: Apenas tenga los resultados, te los mando.
items.english: As soon as I have the results, I'll send them to you.
Call me as soon as you arrive.

sections.title: Order and main verb
sections.content: The time clause can come first or last, and the meaning stays the same: *En cuanto llegue, te llamo* and *Te llamo en cuanto llegue*. The main verb is usually the present, *ir a* + infinitive, the future or a command. The verb in the time clause is the present subjunctive in all of them.

*Apenas* has two jobs. Before a verb, with a second clause after it, it means "as soon as". Next to a verb on its own it means "barely": you know *apenas* "barely" from B2 Unit 1 (*Apenas dormí*). Compare a habit with a single future event: *Cuando llego a casa, cocino* (every day) but *Cuando llegue a casa, cocinaré* (once, later).
